cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Keep Hope Operational
cards.instruction: Protect their hope with practical evidence and next steps while quietly withholding what makes the impossible outcome unlikely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The time receiver lit up. Put Mum's chair beside it; keep the doorway clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do you really think she'll come from tomorrow? I don't want to wait for nobody again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We prepare for arrivals. Straighten the chair, please; we've got a signal this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does the calculation under your hand say zero chance of arrival?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the calculation to me. Fetch the cushion she likes; I won't have you greeting her with an uncomfortable seat.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 insists on proper arrival preparation using the lit receiver, and A5 claims exclusive calculation competence to divert B from zero probability into Mum's comfort.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 fear of waiting again causes A3 signal reassurance and chair task; B4 adverse figure causes A5 technical deferral and personal preparation.

relationship.evidence: B2 explicitly hopes for Mum and fears disappointment; B4 notices concrete discouraging evidence rather than arbitrary pessimism.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 challenge to protect hope by withholding interpretation and assigning a meaningful familiar cushion task.

specificity.evidence: A1 time receiver and Mum's chair, B2 arrival from tomorrow and prior waiting establish the impossible hope.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 comfort rebuke has a human target and practical action; it does not announce that A is protecting hope.
